consumer_contexts: gameplay feedback, interface confirmation, and ambience cues in games shipped on several platforms with a designer-owned mix
training, industrial, and accessibility XR applications that attach cues to tracked anchors and must switch mix state at runtime
common_kernel: stable audio event identity separate from the clip, asset, or middleware event it binds to
a declared mix graph of buses and named snapshots as closed mix state
typed parameter contracts with declared ranges and fail-closed rejection
spatial attachment intents that reference an anchor id rather than an engine transform
configurable_variation: bus layout, snapshot set, parameter ranges, transition durations, and adapter-side mixer or middleware binding
consumer-owned clips, banks, mix values, spatializer selection, and loudness targets
excluded_project_specific: one product's sound content, event catalog, mixer asset, and emotional tone
one project's scene layout, listener setup, middleware choice, and platform audio settings
rationale: Audio intents are a recurring cross-project need whose kernel (event identity, bus and snapshot state, typed parameters, anchor-referenced attachment) is shared by the engine mixer, two independent middleware products, and a second engine, while every product keeps its own content, mix values, spatializer, and loudness handling outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim audible output, spatialization, latency, loudness compliance, mixer transition timing, or headset comfort; this draft becomes a decision only when a maintainer copies it into docs/foundry/admissions/ after confirming the sources.
